item.title: Nagatoro Gorge: Traditional Boat Rides Through Dramatic Rock Cliffs — Guide
item.description: Nagatoro Gorge, where the Arakawa River cuts through a series of distinctive layered rock formations known as Iwadatami (‘rock tatami mats’), is one of Saitama’s most scenic and photographed landscapes, designated a National Natural Monument for its striking crystalline schist cliffs. Traditional wooden boats, operated by local boatmen, carry visitors along a roughly 6 km stretch of the gorge, passing beneath towering rock walls and through gentle rapids, a tradition dating back over a century.
